D: A hobbit sets out from the Shire with a fellowship to destroy a ring of terrible power.
P: Serve the feast at Bilbo's birthday party.
S: Pippin's idea that hobbits need a second breakfast
Thick bacon, fried mushrooms, grilled tomato and buttered toast with marmalade, served mid-morning on a big platter, after the first breakfast.
the hobbits raid Farmer Maggot's crop
Field mushrooms stuffed with garlic, thyme, breadcrumbs and gruyère, roasted at 200C for 15 minutes until bubbling.
the elvish bread from Lothlórien, one bite fills a man

Thick honey and almond shortbread squares scored with a cross, baked pale and wrapped in fresh leaves tied with string. Beat 250g soft butter with 80g caster sugar and 3 tbsp honey until pale. Mix in 300g plain flour, 60g almond meal and a pinch of salt to a soft dough. Press into a lined 20cm square tin, score into 9 squares with a cross on each and prick. Bake at 160C for 35 to 40 minutes until just golden. Cut while warm, cool, then wrap each in a clean banana or vine leaf and tie with kitchen string.
M: the party under the tree with fireworks

Pork shoulder salted overnight and roasted until the crackling shatters, with apple and sage sauce, roast potatoes and buttered cabbage. Score the skin of a 2kg pork shoulder, rub with 1 tbsp salt and leave uncovered in the fridge overnight. Roast at 240C for 30 minutes, then 170C for 2.5 hours. Roast 1kg parboiled potatoes in the fat for the last hour. Simmer 3 chopped apples with 2 tbsp sugar, 30g butter and chopped sage until soft for sauce. Shred half a savoy cabbage and cook in butter for 5 minutes. Rest the pork 20 minutes and carve.
Beef and ale pie: chuck braised in dark ale with onion and thyme for 2.5 hours, under a puff pastry lid, baked at 200C for 25 minutes. Mash and peas.
W: an old-fashioned Shire cake for elevenses
Butter, sugar and eggs creamed, flour and caraway seeds folded in, baked in a loaf tin at 170C for 50 minutes, sliced with butter.
K: it comes in pints at the inn in Bree

Brown ale warmed gently with honey, cinnamon, nutmeg and clove, a knob of butter and an egg yolk whisked through until creamy, served in tankards. Pour 4 bottles of brown ale into a saucepan with 3 tbsp honey, 1 cinnamon stick, 4 cloves and a good grating of nutmeg. Warm over low heat until steaming, never boiling. Whisk 2 egg yolks in a bowl, whisk in a ladle of the hot ale, then whisk it back into the pan with 30g butter and stir for 2 minutes until slightly thickened. Pour into tankards. Use apple juice for a booze-free version.

s.note: Pippin's idea that hobbits need a second breakfast
s.how: Grill 8 rashers of bacon and fry 250g mushrooms in butter. Grill 2 halved tomatoes. Toast 8 slices white bread and butter with marmalade. Serve on a big platter mid-morning. What about elevenses?

s.note: the hobbits raid Farmer Maggot's crop
s.how: Remove the stems from 4 large field mushrooms. Mix 50g breadcrumbs with 2 crushed garlic cloves, thyme, 80g grated gruyère and 30g melted butter. Pile into the caps and roast at 200C for 15 minutes until bubbling.

m.how: Brown 1kg diced beef chuck, add 2 onions, thyme and 375ml dark ale and braise 2.5 hours. Thicken, pour into a dish, top with puff pastry and bake at 200C for 25 minutes. Serve with 1kg potatoes mashed with butter and 300g peas.

w.note: an old-fashioned Shire cake for elevenses
w.how: Beat 175g butter with 175g sugar, add 3 eggs, then fold in 225g self-raising flour, 2 tsp caraway seeds and 3 tbsp milk. Bake in a loaf tin at 170C for 50 minutes. Slice thick and spread with butter.
